title: Omni Models: Qwen2.5-Omni and the Thinker-Talker Split

questions.question: What TTFAB does ttfab(StreamConfig(7, 300, include_vision=True)) return with the default 16kHz microphone?
options: 270 ms, because vision is ignored by the Thinker
350 ms, because the Talker adds no speech decode cost
390 ms, from 50 mic + 180 prefill + 40 first text + 20 Talker + 30 RVQ + 70 waveform
470 ms, because all visual tokens are generated serially twice
questions.explanation: At 16kHz mic_ms=50. A 7B Thinker has 100ms prefill plus 80ms vision cost, first text is 40ms, and the remaining components are 20+30+70ms. The sum is 390ms.

questions.question: What TTFAB does the 7B/200M no-vision configuration in the driver produce?
options: 250 ms
270 ms
350 ms
305 ms, with a 15ms minimum Talker-first stage
questions.explanation: The components are 50ms mic, 100ms prefill, 40ms first text, max(15, 20*200/300)=15ms Talker, 30ms RVQ, and 70ms waveform. Total: 305ms.

questions.question: With silence_threshold_ms=200, which event does simulate_turn_taking place at 4,000ms?
options: VAD triggers the end of the user's turn
The user starts speaking
The Talker emits its first audio
The Thinker finishes the full response
questions.explanation: The simulated user stops at 3,800ms. Adding the 200ms silence threshold yields the VAD end-of-turn event at 4,000ms.

questions.question: Which mode allows the user and model to speak at the same time?
options: Half-duplex, where the active speaker owns the channel
Full-duplex, which supports simultaneous speech and possible backchannels
Turn-taking, which waits for a silence boundary before every token
Batch mode, which emits audio only after the recording ends
questions.explanation: duplex_modes describes full-duplex as simultaneous speaking, unlike half-duplex and VAD-based turn-taking. It is harder because interruption and backchannel behavior must be learned.

questions.question: What does TMRoPE contribute to the Thinker in an omni model?
options: A fixed image-only positional table with no audio axis
A second waveform decoder for residual-VQ layers
A shared timestamp coordinate that aligns vision, audio, and text positions
A vocabulary that removes the need for a Talker
questions.explanation: The lesson describes time-aligned multimodal positions: TMRoPE lets the Thinker relate visual and audio events to text through a common temporal coordinate.

questions.question: What is the defining split in the Qwen2.5-Omni-style design?
options: One encoder for text and a separate database for images
A diffusion image model followed by a speech-only classifier
A single Talker that performs all reasoning and waveform decoding
A large Thinker produces text reasoning tokens while a smaller Talker converts them into streaming speech tokens
questions.explanation: The Thinker consumes multimodal inputs and decides what to say. The Talker consumes its text tokens plus speech context and emits discrete speech tokens for the streaming decoder.
